We use the following standard product inequality: for integers \(n\ge k\ge1\),
\[

\]
Indeed, this is the arithmetic-mean/product comparison applied to the two oppositely ordered sequences \(n,n-1,\ldots,n-k+1\) and \(1,2,\ldots,k\); equivalently, after clearing denominators it is
\[
(k+1)^k n(n-1)\cdots(n-k+1)\ge k!(2n+1-k)^k.
\]
(The case \(k=0\) is immediate.) Therefore
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{n}T_{n,k}\le\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom nk=2^n,
\]
by the binomial theorem. Hence the stated inequality holds for every positive integer \(n\).
